clue.text: Lassie clutches painter, shedding a tear

indicators.note: the lassie holds the other piece inside her, as one clutches something to oneself

parts.note: a wench is an old word for a girl or lass

indicators.note: shedding says the painter loses the following letter

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock painter

explanation.surface: A girl holds onto an artist while shedding a tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' looks like a teardrop, but it is the verb to pull violently; 'Lassie' is not the film dog but a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench something is to pull or twist it away violently, a synonym of tear.

clue.text: Sent message with papers: note enclosed

indicators.note: enclosed says the note sits inside the papers

parts.note: ID, identity papers
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone sent a telegram along with documents and an enclosed note.
explanation.definitionFit: To wire is to send a telegram, so wired means sent a message by telegraph.

clue.text: Cathedral housing this writer's books in particular

indicators.note: the cathedral holds the other pieces inside it as a building houses its contents

parts.note: Ely is the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, standing for its cathedral
the setter refers to themself as this writer, so this writer's is mine
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A cathedral library holds the author's own books specifically.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminently means notably or especially, singling something out, as in particular does.

clue.text: Censor's pet duck?

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O

explanation.surface: Does the official censor keep a duck as a pet?
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder was a Roman censor, the magistrate who oversaw public morals; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Porcius Cato held the Roman office of censor and is known as Cato the Censor.

clue.text: Copper cordoning off large featureless entertainment area

indicators.note: the copper surrounds the next letter as police tape cordons off a scene

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
something featureless is bland

explanation.surface: A policeman seals off a big, characterless leisure zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, which suits 'cordoning off', but it is the element, CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubland is the world or district of nightclubs, a place people go for entertainment.

clue.text: Greener pasture close to edge, tree-covered

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture

indicators.note: covered says the tree wraps around the following letter

parts.note: a fir is a tree

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Pasture near the wooded edge is greener.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafier place has more foliage, so it looks greener.

clue.text: Irritating pong around different things modiste cleared out

indicators.note: around says the pong surrounds the different things

parts.note: BO, body odour, is a pong or bad smell
others means different things

indicators.note: a word cleared out has its inside removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's shop full of odours is unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: A modiste is a dressmaker or milliner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bothersome causes annoyance, so it is irritating.

clue.text: Bow accountant raised capital abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue raised says the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bow is an arc
CA, chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper from Bow in London raised money overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests the London district or a bow of the head; it is an ARC.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana, a foreign capital.

clue.text: Game everyone supports to avoid British

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports goes underneath the others

parts.note: to dodge is to avoid
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A game where everyone backs avoiding the British.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgeball is a playground game where players try to avoid being hit by a thrown ball.

clue.text: Harsh routine in workplace set up

indicators.note: in places the routine within the workplace
in a down clue set up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a lab is a laboratory, a workplace
a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: A tough routine is imposed at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutal means cruel or severe, so it is a synonym for harsh.

clue.text: Rollick and roll around island

indicators.note: around says the roll is placed about the island letter

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Revel and tumble about on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' seems to continue the merrymaking, but it is a list, ROSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, the same boisterous merrymaking as to rollick.

clue.text: Corrective treatment in case of arson cheers police

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's detective police

explanation.surface: Police investigating an arson case get some remedial help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' reads as an investigation, which suits arson and police, but it is the outside of ARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid corrects excess stomach acidity, so it is a remedy that sets the balance right.

clue.text: Attempt perhaps to streamline assembly

definitions.meaning: an attempt to slim one's figure, to streamline
a formal legislative assembly, such as Japan's

explanation.surface: An effort to make a gathering more efficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'streamline' here means make oneself slimmer, with 'perhaps' marking the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is both a slimming regime and a parliament, as in the historic Diet of Worms.

clue.text: Small wheeled vehicle: judge speed of runs?

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a trike is a tricycle
to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: A little tricycle is assessed for how fast it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman's strike rate is runs scored per hundred balls faced; the question mark flags this sports sense of runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Strike rate measures how quickly a cricket batsman scores, the pace at which runs come.

clue.text: Discarding wellie, at home with foot problem?

parts.note: a wellie, a Wellington, is a boot
in means at home
gout often attacks the big toe

explanation.surface: Throwing away a rubber boot because gout keeps the wearer at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A wellie is a British rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Booting out means ejecting or getting rid of, the same as discarding.

clue.text: Sailor slammed Bleriot's substandard work?

parts.note: PO, petty officer, is a naval rank

indicators.note: slammed, as in crashed hard, says the letters of the aviator's name are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A seaman harshly criticises the French aviator's inferior effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slammed' rearranges BLERIOT, the French aviator, into TBOILER; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book or artwork churned out quickly for money, hence of low quality.

clue.text: Orbiter's pilot and guide ultimately crashed

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters are smashed into a new order
ultimately points to the last letter

explanation.surface: An orbiting craft's pilot and navigator ended up crashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges PILOT, AND and E, the last letter of guide; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A planetoid, or asteroid, is a small body that orbits the sun.

clue.text: Back muscles hampering mum's dance

indicators.note: Back says the assembled letters are read in reverse
the muscles get in the mother's way by surrounding her

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Bad back muscles stop a mother from dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like the body part beside muscles, but it is the reversal signal applied after the container is built.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian dance of African origin.

clue.text: Maiden opposing key monster in myth

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
anti means against, opposing
core means key or central

explanation.surface: A girl confronting a vital monster in legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The manticore is a legendary beast with a man's head and a lion's body.

clue.text: A year in decline until now

indicators.note: in places the year letter inside the word for decline

parts.note: to set is to decline or go down, as the sun does

explanation.surface: A year spent going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: As yet means so far, up to the present moment.

clue.text: "Gutsy" mariner departs with very little, scratching head

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: scratching head says the first letter is removed

parts.note: a nominal sum is a very small one

explanation.surface: A brave sailor leaves with almost nothing, scratching his head in puzzlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutsy' in quotes means relating to the guts, not brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominal means relating to the belly, the guts, so a playful reading of gutsy fits.

clue.text: Helper in society located moving north

indicators.note: moving north says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the following words, spread across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An assistant in a society is relocating north.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link, but it is the hidden-word signal; 'moving north' then turns ETYLOCA round, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an assistant, especially one who helps a priest at the altar.

clue.text: Pest you'll find on this flower

definitions.text: Pest you'll find on this flower

parts.words: Pest you'll find on this flower
parts.note: Pest, half of Budapest, stands on the bank of this river, a flower in the crossword sense of something that flows

explanation.surface: A garden pest that lives on a particular bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pest' looks like an insect, but it is the part of Budapest east of the river; 'flower' means something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest straddles the Danube, with Pest on the east bank, so Pest is found on this river.

clue.text: Something like obesity forcing MB into open

indicators.note: forcing the letters together pushes them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A medical graduate is made to talk openly about being overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forcing' rearranges MB, INTO and OPEN together. The surface suggests pushing MB into the word open.
explanation.definitionFit: Embonpoint is a genteel French-derived word for plumpness, a stoutness close to obesity.

clue.text: First couple of breakfast eggs served up well done

indicators.note: the first couple of letters of a word are its first two
in a down clue served up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ova are eggs

explanation.surface: Breakfast eggs served cooked thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well done' looks like a cooking instruction but is praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is a cry of approval, the same as saying well done.

clue.text: Heart of Polish politician yielding

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: The core of a Polish politician is soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital looks like the nationality but simply supplies its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limp is floppy and soft, giving way rather than holding firm.

clue.text: While talking, gathers garden flowers

indicators.note: while talking says the word is heard, not seen spelt

parts.note: to flock is to gather in a crowd

explanation.surface: Someone collects garden blooms while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox are popular garden plants with clusters of fragrant flowers.

clue.text: Dry run during service

indicators.note: during says the run sits within the service

parts.note: aid is help or service
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A practice run during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry run' looks like one phrase, a rehearsal, but 'Dry' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means extremely dry, with little or no rain.

clue.text: Rhetoric from a right-winger on "men"

indicators.note: on places the following pieces after the men, as in an across clue one thing is written on another

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers, the men
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A conservative speaking about men produces fine speechmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, the same skill as rhetoric.

clue.text: Pole, currently Liberal Member of Parliament?

parts.note: a bar is a rod or pole
now means at present, currently

explanation.surface: A Pole is presently a Liberal MP.
explanation.walkthrough: A group of owls is called a parliament, so a barn owl can be a member of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is the collective noun for owls, so any owl belongs to one, as this joke depends on.

clue.text: Lens measures tail of rat in various periods

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take a different arrangement
the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An optician measures lenses at the end of a rat over different eras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges T, the tail of rat, with PERIODS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dioptres are the units of a lens's refractive power, used in spectacle prescriptions.

clue.text: Last words from unclad ladies you kiss

indicators.note: unclad strips a word of its outer letters, its clothing

parts.note: U is text-speak for you
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A man's final words to naked women he is kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unclad' removes the first and last letters of LADIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieux are farewells, the parting words said when leaving.
